channel.title: Jiǎoluò Shūwū · 角落書屋
channel.description: A reading nook for Chinese language and civilisation. Characters, vocabulary, grammar, history, philosophy, and the world they shaped.

item.title: 禅 · meditation; Chan; to abdicate
item.description: One altar character, two civilizations: read shàn it yields thrones and sacrifices to earth; read chán it transliterates Sanskrit dhyāna and founds Zen.

item.title: 星 · star; celestial body; spark
item.description: Born of the sun radical and a sprout, 星 names the stars, the planets, the week, movie fame, and the spark that starts prairie fires.

item.title: 电脑与网络 · Computers & the Internet
item.description: The computer is an electric brain, downloading is "carrying down," and the number 666 is a compliment.

item.title: 度量衡 · Weights & Measures
item.description: Fruit is priced by the half-kilo 斤, distance walks in 里, and an idiom about six of one and half a dozen still counts in base sixteen.

item.title: 看病 · Seeing a Doctor
item.description: Getting sick in Chinese starts with a queue number, runs on the verb "look," and ends with the eternal prescription: drink more hot water.

item.title: 生意 · Doing Business
item.description: Business in Chinese is literally "the meaning of life," merchants are named after a fallen dynasty, and the deal closes at the dinner table.

item.title: 数字系统 · The Chinese Number System
item.description: Chinese numbers are built from eleven syllables and zero irregularity; the catch is that the system pivots on ten thousand, not one thousand.

item.title: 天气 · Talking About the Weather
item.description: Rain falls, wind blows, and fog counts as a noun-verb drama: the small grammar of weather is a beginner's best conversation opener.

item.title: 结果补语 · resultative complements
item.description: Chinese verbs describe the attempt; a second syllable reports the outcome. Listening is 听, but understanding what you heard is 听懂.

item.title: 可能补语 · potential complements
item.description: Slide 得 or 不 inside a verb-result pair and it states ability: 听懂 is understood, 听得懂 is can understand, 听不懂 is the learner's anthem.

item.title: 离合词 · separable verbs
item.description: Words that unzip: 见面 is to meet, but meeting him is 跟他见面 and meeting once is 见一次面, because the "word" is secretly verb plus object.

item.title: 又 · 再 · again, twice over
item.description: Chinese has two agains: 又 looks backward at a repetition that happened, 再 looks forward to one still to come. 再见 is the proof.

item.title: 正反问 · A-not-A questions
item.description: Chinese asks yes-no questions by offering both answers: 去不去 is "going, not going?", and the pattern replaces 吗 with built-in neutrality.

item.title: 工程 · Engineering
item.description: From the carpenter's square inside 工 to the high-speed rail map, the vocabulary of a civilization that has always thought in projects.

item.title: 化学 · Chemistry
item.description: The Chinese periodic table is a naming machine: one character per element, with the radical telling you its state at room temperature.

item.title: 生物 · Biology & the Naming of Living Things
item.description: The panda is a bear-cat, the giraffe a long-necked deer, and the word for gene may be the best translation in the language.

item.title: 数学 · Mathematics
item.description: The vocabulary of Chinese mathematics, where calculus is "tiny accumulation" and geometry was named by a Ming official translating Euclid.

item.title: 天文 · Astronomy
item.description: The five visible planets are named for the five phases, comets are brooms, and the space program borrows its names from mythology.

item.title: 物理 · Physics
item.description: Physics in Chinese is "the pattern of things," a phrase lifted from a Song-dynasty program for investigating the world.

item.title: 多少 · how much, how many
item.description: Chinese builds its "how much" by welding many to few, part of a system where opposites fuse into the scale between them.

item.title: 高兴 · happy, glad
item.description: Happiness as elevation: spirits that rise. The everyday glad word, and how it divides the territory with 开心, 快乐, and 幸福.

item.title: 考试 · examination
item.description: China ran the world's longest experiment in testing, thirteen centuries of imperial exams, and the vocabulary still sits every June for the gaokao.

item.title: 明白 · to understand; clear
item.description: Understanding as illumination: sun-and-moon brightness plus plain white. The clarity verb, and its siblings 懂, 知道, and 了解.

item.title: 声音 · sound; voice
item.description: A chime-stone struck beside an ear: the word for sound welds raw noise to patterned tone, and Chinese theory kept the two distinct.

item.title: 身体 · body; health
item.description: The word for body doubles as the word for health, asking about it is a greeting, and its second character got luckier in simplification than any other.

item.title: 小人 · the petty person
item.description: Confucius took a word that meant "commoner" and turned it into the permanent opposite of the gentleman: the small-hearted schemer of every office.

item.title: 音乐 · music
item.description: Music and joy share a single character, a soulmate is "the one who knows your tone," and the zither smashed for a dead friend still echoes.

item.title: 医院 · hospital
item.description: The healing courtyard: how an arrow wound, a wine jar, and the institutional suffix 院 assembled the word for hospital.

item.title: 饱 · full, satisfied, to eat one's fill
item.description: The food radical 饣 wraps the sound of 包 (bāo), so the glyph itself is a stomach packed full like a dumpling.

item.title: 报 · to report, to announce; newspaper; to repay
item.description: A hand cuffing a kneeling criminal once meant sentencing; today the same glyph carries newspapers, reports, and the moral arithmetic of repayment.
